thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: CUDA_SOFT_OOM detected on pool-gpu-west2 (severity: medium). Auto-suppress attempt started.

pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PDR-29187 opened (service: gpu-inference-prod). Trigger: cuda_soft_oom_rate > 5% over 2m.

alice: acked. I'm on it, switching to oncall rota.

ben: reading metrics now — looks like a KV-cache prefetch spike + a single large customer causing memory churn on pool-gpu-west2.

carla: can we confirm affected model variants? any fallback triggered?

ben: early grep: model variants rtx-7b-q4 and rtx-13b are showing elevated alloc retries. Fallbacks to cpu-infer are limited; autosuppress kicked in but retries persisted.

alice: plan: 1) put pool-gpu-west2 into read-only (drain new requests) 2) scale down prefetchers for that pool 3) route traffic to pool-gpu-east1 and warm standby. Doing 1 now.

ben: executed: kubectl annotate nodepool/gpu-west2 autosuppress=active && curl -s -XPOST https://internal-api/route/drain?pool=gpu-west2 | jq .status

incident-bot: ACTION: autosuppress mode is ON for pool-gpu-west2. New allocations will be throttled.

alice: scaling prefetchers down by 60% (config change pushed).

carla: I pushed a temporary patch to reduce KV prefetch aggressiveness: 
```
PATCH: models/prefetch/config: prefetch_window_ms: 200 -> 50
```
Rolling out canary to 5% first.

dylan: FYI support: one impacting customer reported ~20% of requests had 504s in the last 5m. Raising priority with them.

ben: metrics after throttle: alloc retry rate down from 12% -> 4% in 90s. Latency for fallback paths up slightly.

alice: can we reroute high-qps customers to gpu-east1 now? I'll flip routing rule for tagged customers.

ben: started migration for tag high-qps-cust set. Traffic shift +10% to gpu-east1.

incident-bot: UPDATE: PagerDuty PDR-29187 status: acknowledged by alice.

carla: logs show a spike of tensor allocation failure traces: "CUBLAS_ALLOC_RETRY" not full OOM - soft retries. Looks like fragmentation rather than single allocation too big.

alice: next step: schedule rolling restarts of affected nodes to defragment GPU memory after traffic reduction. Planning 2 nodes at a time.

ben: initiated drain+restart on gpu-west2-node-07 -> restart succeeded, post-restart metrics show reclaimed vmem.

alice: customer-impact update: partial failures for a small subset of requests, mitigated by routing and autosuppress. Support loop engaged.

dylan: sent message to customer: "We're throttling prefetch and shifting traffic to alternate pools; you may see transient elevated latency while we complete restarts." They replied: "thanks, please keep us updated."

carla: keeping watch on KV cache eviction and prefetch logs for 10m.

ben: 10m check: soft-oom alerts dropped to 0.5% rate, autosuppress no longer needed in 2m if steady.

alice: holding until end-to-end SLOs stable. If steady for 15m we'll close PD incident.

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty PDR-29187 will auto-resolve after 30m of no triggers unless manually closed.

alice: marking for manual close pending 20m steady. Good job team. :thumbsup:

carla: follow-up action item: add a prefetch backoff knob tied to KV eviction pressure, and add a dashboard alert for prefetch->alloc_retries correlation.

ben: creating follow-up ticket INFRA-5823 with proposed backoff change and rollback plan.

dylan: customer notified, will follow up with post-incident note.

alice: closing coordination here, staying on watch for the next 10m then I'll close PD. Thanks.

pagerduty: PDR-29187 status: resolved (manual).

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: cuda_soft_oom on pool-gpu-west2 resolved. Postmortem requested.
